results.name: camera_debug_start
results.evidence: Reads a tag-block element indexed by in_AX (stride 0x68) into position/euler globals used by FUN_00444d50 case 0 (debug pov), sets debug mode DAT_006869d2=0, defaults fov, then ticks camera via FUN_00445640(0) and the shake sequence FUN_00447ab0/FUN_00447b50/FUN_00448900.
results.summary: Initializes the debug/free camera state from a camera-point tag element and immediately performs one camera update tick.

results.name: camera_debug_compute_pov
results.evidence: Switches on DAT_006869d2 (0..3): case 0 uses the exact globals set by camera_debug_start (free position/orientation/fov); case 1 calls FUN_006391b4/FUN_004d49b0 (device); case 2 calls object_try_and_get(3) then first-person wrapper FUN_00446d30; case 3 calls object_try_and_get(3) then camera_track_compute_pov (FUN_00445380).
results.summary: Fills a camera pov output struct by dispatching on a 4-way debug camera sub-mode (free, device, first-person, third-person track).

results.name: camera_shake_initialize
results.evidence: Copies a saved per-player camera struct (&DAT_006ac6d0 + in_DX*0xa7, same stride used by camera_get_globals_for_player), then seeds a shake duration/angle/roll using an LCG (DAT_00719cd4 = x*0x19660d+0x3c6ef35f), matching a randomized screen-shake initializer.
results.summary: Seeds a new camera screen-shake effect with randomized duration, angle and roll derived from a linear congruential generator.

results.name: camera_noop_stub
results.evidence: Function body is empty (just returns); 0 callers, no globals or callees referenced. The existing Ghidra name 'physical_memory_initialize' is unrelated to any camera behaviour and the empty body cannot confirm or deny it, so it is likely a spurious match on an identical trivial stub.
results.summary: Empty function that performs no work; true purpose cannot be determined from its body.

results.name: camera_object_cluster_iterator_find
results.evidence: Reads field+0x20 of an object-table entry (param_1&0xffff)*0x200 off the object header table (DAT_0087a480+0x34), then scans data_iterator_next() results comparing their +0x20 field, returning 1 on a match. Called from camera_track_compute_pov (FUN_00445380) alongside camera_iterator_find_or_default.
results.summary: Searches all objects via the data iterator for one whose field at offset 0x20 matches a given object's same field (likely a cluster/parent match).

results.name: camera_iterator_find_or_default
results.evidence: Ghidra flags removed unreachable blocks, indicating lost control flow; the recovered body just drains data_iterator_next() and returns param_2 unchanged. Called right after camera_object_cluster_iterator_find in camera_track_compute_pov to produce a fallback index.
results.summary: Iterates the data object list (decompilation of the real match logic was lost) and returns a value, apparently a found index or the supplied default.

results.name: camera_object_find_best_salt_match
results.evidence: Loops via data_iterator_next() comparing an object's +0x34 and +0x20 fields against caller state and comparing 16-bit 'salt'-like halves (in_stack_00000014 & 0xffff) to find a best index; unrelated to physical memory despite the inherited name 'physical_memory_map_predict_resources'.
results.summary: Scans data objects to find the closest/best-matching object index by salt/generation comparison, falling back to a caller-supplied default.

results.name: camera_track_compute_pov
results.evidence: Builds forward vector from stored yaw/pitch (param_1[3]/[4]), computes up via vector3d_compute_world_relative_right, decays zoom/distance over time using camera_object_cluster_iterator_find/camera_iterator_find_or_default and datum_get to detect cluster/track changes, matching a scripted camera-track chase camera.
results.summary: Computes a chase-camera point of view that follows a scripted camera track/cluster, decaying an initial-approach zoom distance over time.

results.name: camera_initialize
results.evidence: Resets per-player camera state globals (type, shake amount, timer) and sets the active pov function pointer DAT_006ac568 = camera_first_person_compute_pov (FUN_00446d60), then copies default sensitivity settings into 4 per-difficulty slots.
results.summary: Resets the camera subsystem to its default state with first-person as the active camera mode.

results.name: camera_player0_uses_first_person
results.evidence: Loop only ever checks player slot 0 (returns 0 once sVar2>0), then tests whether the mode function pointer table entry equals camera_first_person_compute_pov (FUN_00446d60).
results.summary: Checks whether the first local player's camera is currently in the default first-person mode.

results.name: camera_update
results.evidence: Per-tick entry: stores dt in DAT_006ac558, early-outs with no local player, polls input via camera_poll_look_input, dispatches type changes via camera_select_track_or_type/camera_activate_device_mode, then invokes the active mode function pointer DAT_006ac568(...) to fill a 26-dword pov buffer and blends it into the persistent camera state DAT_006ac5b8.
results.summary: Top-level per-frame camera update: reads input, applies pending mode changes, computes the active camera's point of view via its mode function pointer, and blends it into the live camera state.

results.name: camera_debug_save_to_file
results.evidence: Opens a file via FUN_00624186 and writes DAT_006ac6d0/6d4/6d8 (position), _DAT_006ac6f0.. (forward), _DAT_006ac6fc.. (up) and _DAT_006ac708 (fov) using fprintf("%f %f %f\n", ...).
results.summary: Writes the current debug camera position, forward vector, up vector and fov to a text file.

results.name: camera_debug_load_from_file
results.evidence: Opens a file via FUN_00624186 and reads the same 4 triplets with fscanf("%f %f %f\n", ...) that camera_debug_save_to_file writes, computes an orientation via FUN_00446e30/vector3d_compute_world_relative_right/vector3d_angle_between_4cd4f0, and installs the loaded camera as the active mode (DAT_006ac568=&LAB_00446e90, DAT_006ac560=2).
results.summary: Loads a previously saved debug camera position/orientation from a text file and activates it as the current camera.

results.name: camera_get_type_for_player
results.evidence: Compares the per-player mode function pointer (&DAT_006ac568)[iVar2*0x3e] against camera_first_person_compute_pov (FUN_00446d60, -> type 0), camera_third_person_compute_pov (FUN_00447370, -> type 1), otherwise type 2.
results.summary: Returns an encoded camera type (first-person, third-person, or other) for a given player based on their active mode function pointer.

results.name: camera_get_seat_camera_type
results.evidence: Looks up a unit's seat parent object (field +0x11c), reads a seat-definition entry indexed by the unit's seat index (+0x2f0)*0x11c (same stride used elsewhere for seat/marker blocks) and tests bits (&0x10, &0x40) plus a byte at +0x2a3 against 0x1a/0x1b to pick a camera-type code (1, 2 or 3).
results.summary: Determines which non-default camera type a seated unit should use, based on the vehicle seat's camera-related flags.

results.name: camera_set_type
results.evidence: Calls camera_get_seat_camera_type, and on a type change installs camera_third_person_compute_pov (FUN_00447370) with reset shake fields for type 1, or camera_first_person_compute_pov (FUN_00446d60) otherwise, resetting per-player shake timers (DAT_006ac624/620/564).
results.summary: Applies a camera type change for a player, switching the active pov function pointer between first- and third-person and resetting shake state.

results.name: camera_debug_set_enabled
results.evidence: Writes param_1 through *DAT_0087bc0c; when nonzero installs the debug pov dispatcher camera_debug_compute_pov (FUN_00444d50) and sets DAT_006869d0/DAT_006869d1 (the same debug index/active flag pair written by camera_debug_start); when zero falls back to camera_get_seat_camera_type to restore normal first/third person.
results.summary: Turns the debug camera on or off for a player, switching between the debug pov dispatcher and the normal first/third person camera.

results.name: camera_select_track_or_type
results.evidence: Checks whether the unit's object header has a valid camera_track (offset +0x34 via the object table base DAT_0087a480+0x34, and a short count at +0xae), and if so installs camera_track_compute_pov (FUN_00445380) via camera_shake_initialize (FUN_004450e0); otherwise defers to camera_set_type (FUN_00445c00).
results.summary: Chooses between a scripted camera-track chase camera and the normal first/third-person camera type for a unit, depending on whether it has a camera track.

results.name: camera_activate_device_mode
results.evidence: Calls camera_device_compute_pov (FUN_00446350) then installs &LAB_004464f0 (a related device-camera entry point) as the active mode function pointer, resetting shake state.
results.summary: Switches the active camera to device/cinematic mode.

results.name: camera_poll_look_input
results.evidence: Clears a pov-input buffer, stores camera type and dt, and if network/local-player checks pass, calls FUN_00490b50 eight times to build an 8-bit action mask which is passed to camera_smooth_look_axes (FUN_00446170) along with per-player sensitivity offsets (&DAT_006ac63c/648/654/630).
results.summary: Reads the local player's camera look/zoom input actions and feeds them into the axis smoothing routine, producing yaw/pitch/fov deltas.

results.name: camera_smooth_look_axes
results.evidence: Iterates 4 axis slots applying acceleration/deceleration based on bit flags in param_1 tested against per-axis button indices, clamping the resulting value between stored min/max bounds - a classic analog look-input smoothing loop.
results.summary: Applies per-axis acceleration/deceleration smoothing to camera look input (yaw/pitch/zoom/fov) based on active input flags.

results.name: camera_smooth_look_axes_tail
results.evidence: Body is structurally the same per-axis accel/decel/clamp loop as camera_smooth_look_axes (FUN_00446170), operating on the same unaff_ESI/in_EDX-style registers; 0 callers suggests this is a stray decompiled fragment of that loop rather than an independent 'director/load camera' routine, so the inherited name 'director_load_camera' does not match the code.
results.summary: A duplicate/continuation of the look-axis smoothing loop; despite its inherited name it performs no director or camera-loading logic.

results.name: camera_device_compute_pov
results.evidence: Reads a device transform (DAT_00746f8c+0x354/0x358), computes yaw/pitch via fpatan from its forward vector, writes position+orientation into in_EAX (a pov output), stores it as DAT_006f1814 when param_1==0, and tail-dispatches through a jump table at DAT_00686ab4 indexed by DAT_006f1828.
results.summary: Computes the point of view for the device/cinematic camera from a scripted device transform and dispatches to a per-device follow-up handler.

results.name: camera_device_set_look_target
results.evidence: Stores the passed object index in DAT_00686aa0 and, when the device camera position (DAT_006f1814, set by camera_device_compute_pov) is valid, computes a relative offset (_DAT_006f181c/1820/1824) from it to the target object's position, or to a default axis vector if the target index is -1.
results.summary: Sets the look-at target for the device camera and computes its offset relative to the current device camera position.

results.name: camera_debug_update_transform
results.evidence: Applies input deltas to a camera state array's yaw/pitch/roll (param_1[3..5]) with pitch clamping, rebuilds the forward vector via cos/sin, calls vector3d_normalize_with_length and vector3d_rotate_about_axis for roll, and adds translated movement into the position using object_try_and_get as an optional anchor - the classic free-fly debug camera update.
results.summary: Updates a free-flying debug camera's position and orientation from accumulated look/roll input and movement deltas.

results.name: camera_spectator_compute_pov
results.evidence: Calls chimera__spectate_fp_camera_position() to seed a base position, applies clamped yaw/pitch deltas from param_2, and builds a pov output struct (forward via cos/sin, up via vector3d_compute_world_relative_right/FUN_004f6aa0) similar to the other *_compute_pov functions but with 0 callers, suggesting an alternate/legacy spectator camera path.
results.summary: Computes a spectator-style point of view seeded from the spectate camera position plus accumulated look input.

results.name: first_person_camera_deterministic
results.evidence: Matches the CEA-PDB hint 'first_person_camera_deterministic'; reads the unit's stored camera position (offset +0x23c/+0x240/+0x244) via unit_get_camera_position and, if the unit's weapon has a 'primary trigger' marker (via FUN_004f6080) and a first-person flag on the seat table, overrides the output with the marker's transform - with no matrix/basis rebuild, unlike the '_and_vector' variant.
results.summary: Returns the deterministic first-person camera position for a unit, optionally overridden by its weapon's primary-trigger marker.

results.name: first_person_camera_for_unit_and_vector
results.evidence: Matches the CEA-PDB hint 'first_person_camera_for_unit_and_vector'; builds a basis from an input vector (in_EAX), then for a given unit performs the same primary-trigger-marker lookup as first_person_camera_deterministic but also applies matrix4x3_inverse_transform_normal/matrix4x3_transform_normal to remap the marker orientation into world space.
results.summary: Computes the first-person camera transform for a unit and an accompanying direction vector, using the weapon's primary-trigger marker when present.

results.name: first_person_camera_compute
results.evidence: Thin wrapper that simply calls first_person_camera_for_unit_and_vector (FUN_00446b70) with the caller's register state; used from camera_debug_compute_pov's mode-2 (first-person) case.
results.summary: Forwards to first_person_camera_for_unit_and_vector to compute the first-person camera pov.

results.name: camera_first_person_compute_pov
results.evidence: Installed as DAT_006ac568 by camera_initialize (default mode) and selected as type 0 by camera_get_type_for_player; reads a per-unit zoom value via FUN_00473d70, delegates to first_person_camera_for_unit_and_vector (FUN_00446b70), then reads a fov value via FUN_00471f90 into the output struct.
results.summary: Per-mode pov callback that computes the active first-person camera's transform and field of view for the current unit.

results.name: vector3d_compute_yaw_pitch
results.evidence: Copies a position (in_EDX) then computes yaw = fpatan(y,x) and pitch = fpatan(z, sqrt(x*x+y*y)) from an input vector (in_ECX) into the output pov struct (in_EAX) - used by camera_debug_load_from_file to derive orientation from a loaded forward vector.
results.summary: Converts a position and direction vector into a pov struct's position plus yaw/pitch angles.

results.name: scalar_catmull_rom_interpolate
results.evidence: Explicit 7-float stack parameter list (no register 'unaff_' locals) implementing a non-uniform cubic (Catmull-Rom/Overhauser-style) interpolation formula between param_2/param_3 using neighboring control values param_1/param_4 and knot spacings param_5/param_6/param_7.
results.prototype: double __cdecl scalar_catmull_rom_interpolate(float param_1, float param_2, float param_3, float param_4, float param_5, float param_6, float param_7)
results.summary: Evaluates a non-uniform cubic (Catmull-Rom style) interpolation between two control values given their neighbors and knot spacings.

results.name: vector3d_catmull_rom_interpolate
results.evidence: Calls scalar_catmull_rom_interpolate three times (once per x/y/z component) using four control-point vectors (param_2, unaff_EBX, unaff_EDI, unaff_ESI) and shared knot-spacing parameters, writing the result into param_1.
results.summary: Interpolates a 3D vector between two control points using per-component Catmull-Rom-style cubic interpolation.

results.name: camera_get_trigger_marker_data
results.evidence: Looks up a unit's object header, and if it has a seat-table entry with certain flag bits set (&0x15) returns an offset into that seat's marker block (+0x84); otherwise falls back to a default offset (+0x1a8) off the object's type definition - feeds camera_evaluate_animation_offset.
results.summary: Returns a pointer to a unit's camera-relevant marker/animation data block, from its current seat if applicable, otherwise a default location.

results.name: camera_evaluate_animation_offset
results.evidence: Uses camera_get_trigger_marker_data's block to pick an animation frame index bounded by FUN_006391b4 (frame count) and calls vector3d_catmull_rom_interpolate over consecutive frame vectors to produce an offset, scaled by a normalized angle parameter (param_1).
results.summary: Samples an interpolated offset vector from a unit's marker animation data at a frame chosen from an input angle.

results.name: first_person_camera_apply_weapon_offset
results.evidence: Reads the unit's stored camera position via unit_get_camera_position, obtains a zoom/fov value via FUN_00628630, calls camera_evaluate_animation_offset to get a weapon-relative offset, then rotates and accumulates it into the camera output vector (in_EAX) using the unit's forward/right basis.
results.summary: Adds a weapon-animation-driven offset (e.g. recoil/sway) to the first-person camera position, oriented by the unit's facing.

results.name: camera_third_person_compute_pov
results.evidence: Installed as DAT_006ac568 for camera type 1 by camera_set_type; seeds from chimera__spectate_fp_camera_position, applies clamped yaw/pitch input deltas from a seat data table (DAT_006b145c), computes a distance-scaled orbit offset with camera_evaluate_animation_offset (FUN_00447190) and a collision-adjusted radius via FUN_004f6aa0, matching a classic over-the-shoulder chase camera.
results.summary: Computes the third-person (chase) camera point of view, orbiting the unit at a clamped angle and collision-limited distance.

results.name: real_approximately_equal
results.evidence: Returns true when __isnan(param_1-param_2) is false and |param_1-param_2| < 0.001, a standard epsilon-compare helper (Blam 'real' float type).
results.summary: Returns whether two floating point values are equal within a small epsilon, guarding against NaN.

results.name: real_is_valid
results.evidence: Returns __isnan(param_1)==0, i.e. whether the float is a valid (non-NaN) real number.
results.summary: Checks whether a floating point value is a valid, non-NaN number.

results.name: vector3d_is_unit_length
results.evidence: Computes |x*x+y*y+z*z - 1.0| < 0.001 on an input vector (in_EAX) with a NaN guard, the standard unit-vector validity check.
results.summary: Checks whether a 3D vector is approximately unit length (normalized), guarding against NaN.

results.name: camera_struct_initialize
results.evidence: Fills a large output struct (in_EDX) with default forward/up vectors from PTR_DAT_00696718/00696720, a default fov constant (0x3f5f66f3), zeroes a block of fields, duplicates several vector slots, and writes a repeated magic dword (0x72616421) plus validity byte - consistent with initializing a fresh camera_control-style struct.
results.summary: Initializes a camera output structure with default orientation vectors, field of view, and a validity/magic marker.

results.name: camera_shake_tick
results.evidence: Stores dt in _DAT_006ac658 and, for a valid local player, runs the same shake sequence used in camera_debug_start (camera_shake_blend_targets, camera_shake_advance_splines, camera_shake_apply_to_output), then optionally adds an additional screen-shake offset via FUN_0055cca0 into the player's output position when in default first-person mode.
results.summary: Per-frame entry point that advances and applies the camera screen-shake effect for the local player.

results.name: camera_get_globals_for_player
results.evidence: Returns &DAT_006ac6d0 + in_CX*0xa7 (or NULL for in_CX==-1), the same base/stride used by camera_shake_initialize to index per-player camera state.
results.summary: Returns a pointer to the per-player camera state block for a given player index, or NULL if the index is invalid.

results.name: vector3d_compute_world_relative_right
results.evidence: Normalizes the horizontal (x,y) projection of an input forward vector (unaff_ESI) via vector3d_normalize_with_length, then cross-multiplies it back against the full forward vector to produce a perpendicular vector in unaff_EDI - used throughout the module wherever a camera basis is built from a forward vector.
results.summary: Derives a world-relative perpendicular (right/up-family) vector from a camera forward vector using its horizontal projection.

results.name: camera_shake_blend_targets
results.evidence: For each of 5 shake channels, blends a stored target value (&DAT_006ac6b8) into a working buffer (&DAT_006ac660) with a 2.0 clamp when validity/override bits in a flags byte are set, then copies the whole 26-dword struct to a secondary buffer (&DAT_006ac664).
results.summary: Blends newly requested shake target values into the active shake state buffer prior to spline evaluation.

results.name: camera_shake_advance_splines
results.evidence: Guarded by a 'settled' flag bit (&0x20) on the shake buffer, calls the five spline-related helpers (camera_shake_compute_relative_orientation, camera_shake_compute_spline_coefficients, camera_shake_evaluate_spline_derivative, camera_shake_evaluate_spline_position, camera_shake_apply_and_orthonormalize) then decays 5 channel values by the frame's shake time _DAT_006ac658.
results.summary: Advances the camera shake spline for the current frame across all shake channels and decays their remaining time.

results.name: camera_shake_compute_spline_coefficients
results.evidence: For 5 shake groups, derives cubic Hermite-style coefficients (using constants 0.5, 3.0, 4.0, 6.0, 7.0, 10.0, 15.0, 20.0 typical of quintic/Hermite basis derivatives) from position/velocity/acceleration input arrays into 6 output coefficient arrays per group.
results.summary: Computes per-channel polynomial (spline) coefficients for the camera shake curve from its current position, velocity and target.

results.name: camera_shake_evaluate_spline_derivative
results.evidence: For each of 5 groups, evaluates a cubic-derivative-style polynomial (2*a + 6*t*b + 12*t^2*c + 20*t^3*d) using the coefficients from camera_shake_compute_spline_coefficients, zeroing channels once the local time exceeds the shake duration _DAT_006ac658.
results.summary: Evaluates the rate-of-change (derivative) of the camera shake spline for each channel at the current local time.

results.name: camera_shake_evaluate_spline_position
results.evidence: For each of 5 groups, evaluates a quintic-style position polynomial (2*t*a + 3*t^2*b + 4*t^3*c + 5*t^4*d + e) from the same coefficient arrays, with special-case handling (negate/zero) when a channel flag bit indicates the shake has settled.
results.summary: Evaluates the camera shake spline's position value for each channel at the current local time.

results.name: camera_shake_apply_and_orthonormalize
results.evidence: Evaluates a further quintic position term per channel into an accumulator, occasionally routing through camera_shake_apply_axis_angle_rotation (FUN_00448880) once 4 channels have accumulated, then re-orthonormalizes the resulting basis vectors (&DAT_006ac72c/730/734 and &DAT_006ac738/73c/740) via cross products and normalization, guarded by __isnan/epsilon checks.
results.summary: Accumulates evaluated shake displacement into the camera orientation basis and re-orthonormalizes the resulting axes.

results.name: camera_shake_compute_relative_orientation
results.evidence: Subtracts two position arrays (in_EAX-in_ECX) then loops computing a relative transform (matrix4x3_inverse, matrix4x3_multiply via PTR_matrix4x3_multiply_00696664, quaternion_from_matrix4x3) and converts the resulting quaternion axis into a scaled axis-angle vector via fpatan.
results.summary: Computes the relative rotation between two transforms and expresses it as a scaled axis-angle vector for shake blending.

results.name: camera_shake_apply_axis_angle_rotation
results.evidence: Normalizes an input vector via vector3d_normalize_with_length to get a rotation angle, and if nonzero rotates two vectors about that axis via vector3d_rotate_about_axis - called from camera_shake_apply_and_orthonormalize to fold accumulated rotation into the shake basis.
results.summary: Rotates a pair of basis vectors about an axis-angle vector, used to apply accumulated shake rotation.

results.name: camera_shake_apply_to_output
results.evidence: Reads the evaluated shake position/orientation buffers (&DAT_006ac70c..), clamps them, applies a horizontal rotation by the camera's own facing, optionally corrects for collision via camera_third_person_avoid_collision (FUN_00448d40) when not flagged (&0x10), updates the player's cluster index via FUN_005013a0, clamps final values to +/-5000, and writes the finished position/forward/up/fov into the per-player camera output block (&DAT_006ac6d0.. via camera_get_globals_for_player's stride).
results.summary: Combines the evaluated camera shake result with the base camera transform, applies collision correction, and commits the final position/orientation/fov to the active per-player camera output.

results.name: camera_third_person_avoid_collision
results.evidence: Casts rays (up to 4 offset directions plus a 10-iteration binary search) via FUN_00505880 with flags 0x40e1/0x40a1 between the camera anchor and a target point scaled by *param_3 (a distance/zoom value), shrinking *param_3 toward the nearest unobstructed fraction found - a classic third-person camera collision pull-in.
results.summary: Adjusts the third-person camera's follow distance to avoid clipping through world geometry, using ray casts and a binary search for the nearest safe distance.

results.name: camera_collision_test_ray
results.evidence: Thin wrapper selecting one of two collision-test flag values (0x40e1/0x40a1 - the same pair used by camera_third_person_avoid_collision) based on in_DL, then calls FUN_00505880 once and returns whether the ray hit along with the hit fraction.
results.summary: Performs a single collision ray test used by the third-person camera's collision-avoidance logic.
